gen-zen-dots-gf-akatab: Akatab has round, cupped letters that feel approachable. Under Zen Dots, with its generous space around every shape, a long block of text stays easygoing and never feels pinched or hurried.
gen-zen-dots-gf-alan-sans: Alan Sans reads modern and businesslike, its curve tails held well back from the body. Zen Dots hands over a techy, friendly heading, and Alan Sans then carries a long passage smoothly, with a polished, steady feel.
gen-zen-dots-gf-albert-sans: Contemporary and professional, Albert Sans keeps its openings clear even when tiny. Zen Dots is the thin, wire-drawn heading, so if the heading looks faint, nudge it larger and let the body stay modest.
gen-zen-dots-gf-alef: Zen Dots brings a friendly, techy heading with generous space around each shape. Alef follows in clean sans-serif, its open-ended curves making a long passage feel modern and unfussy.
gen-zen-dots-gf-alegreya-sans-sc: Wide-open spacing around every letter defines Zen Dots, a techy display face that stays friendly. Alegreya Sans SC follows with a welcoming gap in its c, so a long passage reads modern and inviting.
gen-zen-dots-gf-almarai: Techy, friendly, and light as pencil lines. Zen Dots sketches the heading in thin strokes, and Almarai's plain sans body holds one steady line width, so give the heading extra size.
gen-zen-dots-gf-amarna: Zen Dots gives every letter generous space. Amarna's strokes run like bent copper pipe, so the thin heading and tubular sans body feel like cousins on the page.
gen-zen-dots-gf-andika: Zen Dots is a thin, wire-like heading with generous room around each letter shape. Make it small and it fades beside Andika's sturdy sans.
gen-zen-dots-gf-anta: Friendly and techy, Zen Dots draws its heading like a drafting pen. Anta, in sans-serif with gaping e shapes and constant thickness, keeps a longer stretch of text open and approachable.
gen-zen-dots-gf-antic: Zen Dots is a tech-flavored display face that loves space around its letters, a thin-lined heading with real personality. But Antic does the quieter work, its sans strokes held to one nib and its mouths left open for steady reading.
